topics.label: Introduction and Learning Outcomes
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer introduces the final lecture of the course and sets out the learning objectives regarding cancer therapy approaches.

topics.label: Traditional Therapies: Surgery, Radiotherapy, and Cytotoxic Chemotherapy
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine conventional cancer treatment modalities, detailing how surgical resection, radiation, and cytotoxic drugs eliminate rapidly dividing cells and the clinical limitations associated with them.

topics.label: Exploiting Tumor Vulnerabilities, Checkpoint Defects, and DNA Repair Deficiencies
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore therapeutic strategies that exploit intrinsic biological vulnerabilities in cancer cells, including hormone dependence, cell cycle checkpoint loss, and synthetic lethality from DNA repair defects.

topics.label: Oncogene Addiction, Kinase Inhibitors, and Drug Resistance
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics focus on the identification of driving oncogenes, the development of small-molecule kinase inhibitors targeting ATP-binding clefts, and the genetic and pathway-level mechanisms of drug resistance.

topics.label: Monoclonal Antibodies and Antibody-Drug Conjugates
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics discuss therapeutic strategies that use engineered antibodies to directly target tumor surface antigens or deliver cytotoxic payloads into cancer cells.

topics.label: Harnessing the Immune System and T-Cell Therapies
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics detail the mechanisms and applications of immunotherapy, ranging from immune checkpoint inhibitors to bispecific T-cell engagers and chimeric antigen receptor T-cell therapies.

topics.label: Systemic Challenges, Clinical Progress, and Future Directions
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics review the major challenges in oncology, historical improvements in patient survival, and emerging future paradigms such as early detection, genomic profiling, and ethical considerations in treatment.
